government.note: Parliamentary republic under the 1991 Constitution. Executive authority is vested in the Government headed by the Prime Minister, who is elected by the National Assembly; the directly elected President (five-year term, two consecutive terms at most) has a largely ceremonial role. The 90-member National Assembly is the legislature proper. The 40-member National Council (Državni svet), indirectly elected by local and interest-group electors, has an advisory role and a suspensive veto; it is not modelled as a chamber here. Laws passed by the National Assembly can be put to a legislative referendum on the demand of 40,000 voters; a law is rejected only if a majority votes against and the votes against amount to at least one fifth of registered voters (rule since 2013).

system.note: 88 seats by list PR in eight constituencies (D'Hondt), plus one seat each for the Italian and Hungarian national communities (Borda count). The threshold was 3.2% (three seats) in 1996 and has been 4% since 2000. seats_2000 is the result of the November 1996 election; changes between 1996 and 1 January 2000 were not checked. The two minority members are counted under 'others'.

start_2000.ideology_support_note: Derived from the November 1996 National Assembly vote (shares computed from the vote counts): LDS 27.0% (social liberal), SLS 19.4% (agrarian), SDS (then SDSS) 16.1% (recorded with the party's later national-conservative profile), SKD 9.6% (Christian democrat), ZLSD 9.0% (social democrat), DeSUS 4.3% (pensioners' party, recorded as big tent), SNS 3.2% (right populist), Democratic Party 2.7% (centrist liberal), Greens of Slovenia 1.8% and Green Alternative 0.5% (green), Liberal Party 0.7% (classical liberal), Communist Party 0.5% (Marxist-Leninist); the remaining small lists and independents (about 5.1%) are assigned to liberal conservative.
